 RAC no more relevant in digital ticket-checking era: Railway officials say old reservation rule under review as vacant berths can now be allotted faster
 SECTIONS RAC no more relevant in digital ticket-checking era: Railway officials say old reservation rule under review as vacant berths can now be allotted faster ET Online Last Updated: Nov 18, 2026, 04:54:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Indian Railways may scrap the Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) facility as senior officials believe digital ticketing and tracking systems have reduced its relevance. Under RAC, two passengers share one berth while paying the full fare. The proposal has also raised questions about fare refunds, vacant berths and passenger convenience. Here is why railway officials want to end the decades-old system and what it could mean for passengers.
 iStock Train RAC facility has outlived its utility in era of digital ticket checking: Railway officials
 Indian Railways may do away with the Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) facility, which allows two passengers to share a single berth during a train journey. According to a PTI report, a section of senior railway officials believes the system has lost its relevance because of improvements in digital ticketing and reservation systems. RAC was introduced to help passengers travel even when confirmed berths were unavailable. However, officials now argue that digital tools allow vacant berths to be identified and allotted to other passengers more quickly, reducing the need for the arrangement.
 The proposal could also bring changes to how passengers are charged when they are not allotted a full berth despite paying the full fare.

 What is the RAC system in Indian Railways?
Under the RAC system, two passengers share one berth, with each paying the full ticket fare. They are allowed to travel, but do not get a full berth each unless one becomes available.
The facility was introduced in 1983-84 by then Railway Minister ABA Ghani Khan Choudhury during his Railway Budget speech in Parliament.
 Live Events
 At the time, Choudhury said a fixed number of berths would be reserved for senior-most passengers on the waiting list. These passengers could then be given full berths during the journey if passengers with confirmed tickets failed to turn up.
 Read more - Bengaluru taxi drivers are unhappy as Vietnam's Green SM plans 10,000 electric cabs with fares as low as Rs 8 per km 
 The system was also intended to prevent arbitrary allotment of vacant berths by railway staff.
 How did Indian Railways expand RAC berths in 2016?
Indian Railways revised the RAC arrangement in 2016 and increased the number of berths reserved for such passengers.
The changes covered sleeper, 3AC and 2AC coaches.
 Sleeper class: Side-lower berths reserved for RAC passengers increased from five to seven per coach. This raised the number of passengers accommodated from 10 to 14.
 3AC: RAC berths increased from two to four side-lower berths per coach, allowing eight passengers instead of four.
 2AC: The number of reserved berths increased from two to three side-lower berths per coach, taking the passenger capacity from four to six.
 Why do railway officials want to scrap RAC now?
According to PTI, some senior railway officials believe digital ticketing and checking systems have reduced the need for RAC.
Earlier, identifying vacant berths and allotting them to passengers could involve manual processes. Now, train ticket examiners (TTEs) use Hand Held Terminals (HHTs), which are connected to the railway reservation system.
If a passenger with a confirmed ticket does not turn up, the TTE can mark the passenger as a no-show on the device. The vacant berth can then be made available to other passengers from the next station.
A senior railway official told PTI that the digital system has changed the way vacant berths are managed. Officials also believe scrapping RAC could reduce the scope for unfair practices by limiting the discretionary powers of TTEs.
They argue that this would encourage ticket examiners to complete checks on time and update the system so that vacant berths can be offered to other passengers.
 Why does Indian Railways not lose money when passengers fail to turn up?
Another argument being made in favour of scrapping RAC is that the Railways does not lose the fare when a passenger with a confirmed ticket fails to board the train.
Under the cancellation rules introduced in 2015, passengers who do not turn up for their journey forfeit the entire fare paid. They do not receive a refund.
The Railways can then offer the vacant berth to another passenger at the next station, who pays the applicable fare.
A senior railway official told PTI that the Railways has already collected the fare from the original passenger. Therefore, even if that passenger does not travel, there is no financial loss to the national transporter. The vacant berth can also be used by another passenger instead of remaining empty.
 What did the Parliamentary panel say about RAC fares?
The RAC system has also faced criticism over passengers paying the full fare despite sharing a berth.
In a report presented in the Lok Sabha on February 4, 2026, the Parliamentary Public Accounts Committee questioned the practice of charging the full fare when an RAC passenger was not allotted a full berth even after the reservation chart was prepared.
The committee said this was not justified and recommended that the Railway Ministry develop a system to provide partial refunds to such passengers.
However, railway officials have pointed out that implementing refunds could be complicated. Passengers book tickets through online platforms as well as at physical reservation counters, making it difficult to create a common refund mechanism.
 Which trains do not have the RAC facility?
At present, Vande Bharat Sleeper trains do not offer the RAC facility. Passengers are allotted confirmed berths or waitlisted tickets, rather than sharing a berth under the RAC arrangement.
The fares of Vande Bharat Sleeper trains are also 30% to 95% higher than those of other trains operating on the same routes.
For now, the Railway Ministry has not announced a final decision on scrapping RAC. If the proposal moves forward, it could change how passengers with waitlisted tickets are accommodated and how vacant berths are allotted during train journeys.
 Inputs from PTI
